name: workspace.listFolder
title: List folder
summary: The folders and links, and on request the files, in the folder of a typed path, for completing a path while it is typed.
details: The text up to its last separator (`/`, and `\` on Windows) names the folder, the rest is the typed name. A relative path is resolved from the workspace root on every access, also on the command line; `~` stands for the home folder as in the path arguments of the access (in the app; the command line and API and MCP take it as an ordinary name), and with `absolute` on every access, where the path must then be absolute. The path is checked by its text first: a UNC, device or NT path, a path on the current drive, a Windows device name, NUL or more than 4096 characters gives `invalid` without any file-system call. Through the API and the MCP server the folder must lie inside the repositories of the workspace (SR-142). Only the entries of the folder are read: no link is resolved, so a link is listed by its name. Where the file system gives no entry type with the names (NFS without readdirplus, some FUSE file systems, XFS without ftype), listing a large folder can take longer than its 1 s bound.

path.description: The typed path, up to the name being typed (`~/pro`, `out/`, `C:\Work\sp`). A plain text, not a `localPath`: it is taken as typed, with its separator at the end.

files.description: Also list the files (for an argument that takes a file); folders and links are always listed.

absolute.description: Take only an absolute path, with `~` and `~/…` for the home folder on every access ("Open workspace", SR-131); without it the path is resolved as the commands of the access resolve a path argument: `~` is the home folder in the app only.

folder.description: The folder listed, absolute and normalised, without a separator at its end except at the root. Missing when the path is `invalid`.

name.description: The typed name: the text after the last separator. Names that start with "." are listed only when it starts with ".".
The name as the file system spells it.

kind.description: folder, file, or link: a symbolic link, and on Windows any reparse point (junctions, OneDrive and Cloud Files placeholders, deduplicated files, app execution aliases); its target is not looked at.

entries.description: The entries, folders and links first, then files, each by the code units of the NFC form of the name. Other entries (sockets, devices) are left out. Empty with a `problem`.

problem.description: Why there are no entries: the folder does not exist (`missing`), cannot be read or gave no answer within 1 s (`unreadable`, also when the path names a file), or the path is refused by its text (`invalid`).

truncated.description: The folder has more than 50,000 matching entries; folders and links come first.
